> Uses a deterministic TinyShakespeare excerpt generated from Project Gutenberg with an explicit cross-entropy target, making it suitable for classroom training correctness and public performance reporting.

## At a Glance

| **Field** | **Value** |
|:---|:---|
| **Suite** | language |
| **Model** | nanogpt-12m |
| **Parameters** | 11.5M |
| **Dataset** | tinyshakespeare |
| **Dataset source** | Project Gutenberg eBook 100, generated MLPerf EDU tiny Shakespeare excerpt, character-level, 1.1MB |
| **Scenario** | single_stream |
| **Maturity** | base |
| **Public status** | score-bearing |
| **Provenance** | Vaswani et al. 2017 (Transformer); maps to MLPerf Training GPT-3/LLaMA |

> **Parameter count note:** Char-level vocab=128 (TinyShakespeare uses 65 unique chars). Earlier README/paper figures of 85.9M and 124.4M reflected a vocab=50,257 BPE config that was never reachable from the char-level data; iteration 1 reconciled the model to its actual effective size. As built (vocab=128, n_embd=384, n_head=6, n_layer=6, max_seq_len=2048, tied wte/lm_head) the base model instantiates 11,483,136 parameters; re-derive this figure if the base max_seq_len changes.

## How to Run

```bash
# one-time asset preparation
mlperf fetch --workload nanogpt-train --profile max

# benchmark run (writes JSON/HTML/CSV reports + .provd provenance)
mlperf run --workload nanogpt-train --profile max --open-report

# quick smoke pass
mlperf run --workload nanogpt-train --profile min

# research envelope
mlperf run --workload nanogpt-train --profile pro
```

See the [running guide](../../guide/running.qmd) for profile semantics, report handling, and power measurement flags.

## Measured Systems Regime

**Working set:**

| **Field** | **Value** |
|:---|:---|
| **Value** | unmeasured |
| **Peak bytes per step** | 67108864 |
| **Note** | Per-layer activation peak ~12 MB at B=16 T=64. Training reads all ~46 MB of fp32 weights and writes gradients plus Adam moment state on every optimizer step (~100 steps per epoch at the defaults), so per-epoch weight traffic is roughly 100x the weight bytes plus optimizer-state traffic, not a single per-epoch stream. Per-step resident set falls in the 6-48 MB grey band; exact classification depends on batch size and caching behavior — measure with cache-miss counters. |
